name: LetterGlitch-TS-TW

frames.best_why: The glyph wall spreads evenly with a clear mix of green, teal and blue characters.

tagline: A dense wall of tiny letters flickers like a broken terminal.
summary: Thousands of small monospace characters and symbols fill a black panel in rows. Scattered glyphs swap to new characters every moment and fade between green, teal and blue.
appearance: Even rows of short monospace characters, letters, digits and punctuation, packed across a black surface. Text runs in three muted tones, sage green, mint and steel blue, with a dark vignette pulling the corners down.
behaviour: At a steady tick a small share of the characters change to random symbols and take on a new colour, easing across rather than snapping if smoothing is on. Everything else stays put, so the field shimmers instead of scrolling.
use_when: A dev or security themed hero needs a dense text texture behind the copy.
avoid_when: Long-form reading or light themes: the small glyphs add visual noise and the surface is fixed black.
customise: The three glitch colours, tick speed, character set, smoothing and either vignette can be set. Font size and the share of letters changed each tick are fixed in the source.
weight_why: A canvas of hundreds of glyphs redraws about twenty times a second.

a11y.note: A decorative canvas with no text alternative and no reduced-motion check, so the flicker never stops.

issues: At this density the glyphs read as texture rather than legible text, and the colours are low contrast.
polish_why: A competent matrix-style texture; the effect is familiar and the palette is dim.
